user.title: Add an E-ink Renderer
user.description:
Enter the address of the computer running eink-renderer, for example `192.168.0.50` or `192.168.0.50:10001`.

Renderers on the same network usually appear on their own under **Discovered**, so you may not need this.

setup.title: Set up {name}
setup.description: Found at `{host}`. Choose what the display should show and which display it is. Contrast, colours and theme have good defaults and can be changed later with **Configure**.{locked}

custom_size.title: Display size
custom_size.description: Size of the display in pixels.

preview.title: This is what your display will show
preview.description:
![Preview of the e-ink image]({preview})

{view}, {size} pixels.{note} If it looks right, submit to finish. You can change the view, contrast and theme later with **Configure**.

Your display will fetch `{url}`.

problem.title: The renderer can't show the dashboard yet
problem.description:
{problem}

If the renderer cannot reach Home Assistant, correct the address below (it must work from the renderer's computer) and try again.

data.ha_url: Home Assistant address, as seen by the renderer

reauth_confirm.title: Pair {name} again
reauth_confirm.description: The renderer has forgotten its pairing, for example because its data volume was reset. Submit to pair it again; your settings stay as they are.

progress.render: Paired. Waiting for the first image; this usually takes less than 10 seconds.

error.cannot_connect: {error} Check the address and port (the default port is 10001) and that the renderer container is running.
error.not_a_renderer: That address answers, but it is not an eink-renderer. {error}
error.already_paired: This renderer is already paired with another Home Assistant. If that wasn't you, reset it on its host with `docker exec eink-renderer eink-renderer --reset-pairing` (use your container's name), restart the container and try again.
error.no_storage: This renderer has no data volume, so it cannot remember the pairing. Start it with `-v eink-data:/data`.

abort.already_configured: This renderer is already set up.
abort.cannot_connect: The renderer stopped answering. Check that it is running and try again.
abort.not_a_renderer: This device does not identify itself as an eink-renderer.
abort.already_paired: This renderer is already paired with another Home Assistant. To pair it with this one, run `docker exec eink-renderer eink-renderer --reset-pairing` on its host (use your container's name), restart the container, then add it again.
abort.no_storage: This renderer has no data volume, so it cannot remember the pairing. Start it with `-v eink-data:/data` and add it again.

create_entry.esphome:
Done: the renderer is paired and rendering. The **E-ink** sidebar panel shows it next to the live dashboard.

For your ESPHome display, use this `online_image` block (the image URL is `{url}`):

```yaml
{esphome}```
